Login button · five pages, five copies
home.css .login { background: var(--text-3); } pricing.css .login { background: var(--text-3); } blog.css .login { background: var(--text-3); } docs.css .login { background: var(--text-3); } app.css .login { background: var(--text-3); }

HomeLog in

DocsLog in

Example: the same button style lives in five files. Updating its color means finding and changing each copy.

What repeated code can change

Before: five files keep separate copies: Changing the button color means finding five definitions; miss Docs and its button stays gray.

The change: a shared component: Following the project's existing structure, put the button style in one shared component and let all five pages use it.

Feedback and boundary: Reopen all five pages and confirm the buttons are blue without changing other page behavior. Whether to consolidate more depends on the actual maintenance burden; not every repeated line needs rewriting.

What people often confuse

Not every repeated line needs consolidation. When a color update has already missed one page and still means finding five sources, the maintenance burden is visible. Before sharing an implementation, check whether any page needs its own style.
